title: Ryazan refinery struck again — Isomal-2 isomerization unit knocked out
detail: Ukrainian FP-1 drones struck Russia's Ryazan oil refinery (Rosneft) overnight, hitting the Izomalk-2-LIN-800 low-temperature isomerization unit that converts low-octane straight-run fractions into the high-octane blending component needed for Euro-5 gasoline. The strike is the latest in a pattern of repeated attacks on the refinery — struck at least 9 times since August 2025 — and lands on a plant already crippled: two of its four primary crude distillation units (ELOU-AVT-6 and AVT-3, together over 77% of primary processing capacity) were already offline from earlier strikes, with August satellite imagery showing roughly half the plant's primary distillation capacity out of action. Ryazan accounts for about 5% of Russia's national refining capacity. Regional governor Pavel Malkov said there were no casualties and that emergency services were working at the site. The same night, drones also struck an airfield, a radar station and two Pantsir-S1 air defense systems in Rostov region, damaging a residential building in Rostov-on-Don. A Sept 10 Reuters report citing industry sources gave a fuller damage picture: the strike also forced offline the refinery's CDU-6 unit (roughly 8 million tonnes/year, or about 160,000 bpd — around half of Ryazan's total capacity — which caught fire) and the smaller CDU-4 unit, with repairs expected to take several weeks; a third unit, CDU-3, had already been under maintenance since mid-May.

media.caption: Fire at Ryazan oil refinery after a Ukrainian drone strike hit the Isomal-2 isomerization unit, Sept 6, 2026
